rows.required_scope: The conductor-one character cuts out F_D and its unaveraged point belongs to E(F_D); the rational components are D and hstar.
rows.connecting_reason: The retained relative-discriminant calculation identifies the unramified character of Gal(H/K) as chi_hstar composed with ideal norm. Reindexing the finite unaveraged sum by an Artin class b gives b(P_D)=chi(b)P_D. Hence the kernel fixes P_D, so P_D belongs to E(F_D). For D>1 the two rational characters of Gal(F_D/Q) restricting to this nontrivial character of Gal(F_D/K_D) are chi_D and chi_hstar. This is a statement about E(F_D) tensor Q; no integral idempotent denominators are suppressed. For D=1, F_D=K_D and the two characters are the trivial character and chi_hstar.
rows.boundary: Requires the actual conductor-one CM point over H and its Artin action, as supplied by the separate CM construction. The field formula is not deduced from the height theorem.

rows.required_scope: The hstar-twist rational component is torsion because its analytic rank is zero.
rows.connecting_reason: Apply the existing forward theorem to A=E^(hstar), whose central L-value was chosen nonzero. Rank zero means this character component vanishes after tensoring with Q.
rows.boundary: Does not infer rank from the genus field or use a converse theorem; the height nonvanishing is a separate existing CST input.

rows.required_scope: One fixed C_pi kills all cusp translations, and L is chosen divisible by 4 B C_pi.
rows.connecting_reason: Use the same fixed based modular parametrization and its already established finite cuspidal image. The actual involutions permute cusps, so pi(W infinity) is in that image. The subsequent integral character operator and torsion annihilator B are the displayed local calculation.
rows.boundary: The value pi(infinity)=0 alone does not kill pi(W infinity); no bounded degree torsion statement is inferred from Manin–Drinfeld.

rows.required_scope: The good-prime Hecke correspondence and the based quotient identity specialize to the same modular and elliptic models.
rows.connecting_reason: For p not dividing N*ell0, the good correspondence is represented by adjoining a cyclic p-subgroup to the N-level object. Since p is invertible at ell0, these subgroups are finite etale and quotienting preserves the coprime N-level structure. Thus the two degeneracy maps exist over the same good base. The generic based-quotient identity and T_p(infinity)=(p+1)infinity extend there by separatedness; the correspondence counts p-neighbors with their usual multiplicities. The fixed map extends by the retained Neron mapping argument. Its reduction therefore satisfies the displayed sum identity. The Atkin constant is killed by the already chosen L; actual Atkin eigen-action and the separate global geometric identification remain inputs.
rows.boundary: This gives no good-reduction statement at primes dividing pN and no descent of chosen enhanced models. The following separate row binds the supplied lambda_M and its Frobenius invariance.

rows.required_scope: The finite function P_M has the stated good Hecke, Atkin and right-uniformizer eigenvalues.
rows.connecting_reason: The additive functional lambda_M is Frobenius invariant by its explicit Kummer construction and bC=b. Compose it with the specialized good-Hecke identity; apply the already supplied Atkin eigen-action, and annihilate the cusp translation because L is a multiple of C_pi. Ribet identifies right division-uniformizer action with Frobenius.
rows.boundary: The actual Atkin operator identification and eigen-action remain separately accepted source inputs; the local matrix model alone does not establish a global correspondence.
